method: Verified all assigned file SHA-256 values against ROOT snapshot. Enumerated every unchecked key from S01.json, reviewed its full extracted task text and corresponding source line/context; checked JEV/toolkit references against the accepted typed-decision handoff and APP implementation. No task in this shard benefits from replacing measurement, deterministic verification, kernel code, or human authority with Jev: local typed choice primitives do not speed CPU/GPU kernels, establish performance, authorize a production change, or produce independent benchmark evidence. Semantic review identified CS-24 as a genuine closed-set classification use of the shipped JEV stack; no other recommendation substitutes typed decisions for measurement, deterministic verification, kernel correctness, or human authority. No inference/build/reload/process action. its implementation option is shadow-only and its CS-4 comparative evaluation remains inference-gated. CS-18’s retain/cancel behavior is already an explicit deterministic host policy, so adding JEV there would duplicate a settled rule.

findings.title: Use the existing typed-decision runner as CS-24 option (ii)
findings.original_premise: CS-24 compares three voice-turn routing mechanisms (prompt policy, short first-pass classification, parallel text classifier) on CS-4 routing clips, but option (ii) leaves the output shape and failure handling unspecified.
findings.revised_deliverable: Specify option (ii) as a local one-question `QuestionKind.CHOICE` classifier over the closed routing labels for social/non-social (and an explicit unknown/abstain outcome only if the CS-4 annotation contract supports it). Use `run_typed_decisions` and the existing typed shadow logger to record output beside the incumbent decision; keep actual routing on the incumbent host policy. Add deterministic mocked-primitive cases for valid label, invalid schema/transport failure, and unknown/ambiguous input. Preserve the original three-arm comparison and precision/recall gate on CS-4; include latency/call-cost so the extra pass is priced.

toolkit_reuse.what: Closed candidate labels and explicit parse failures, suitable for option (ii); confidence is an uncalibrated statistic.
Local one-pass typed call with Draft 2020-12 schema validation and explicit failure records.
Default-off, bounded asynchronous, fail-open shadow call that records typed output and incumbent without changing the route.
Existing default-off feature gate for shadow instrumentation.

source_evidence.observation: CS-24 offers prompt policy, short first-pass classification, or parallel text classifier and requires precision/recall on CS-4 routing set; CS-41 consumes logged decisions.
Generic shadow path records typed questions, incumbent, failures, and latency; it is default-off, async, bounded, and does not alter incumbent.
Question supports choice over unique labels; DecisionResult retains failures and confidence is a local, uncalibrated statistic.
Runner performs schema-validated local typed decisions and preserves failures.

findings.non_inference_scope: Add the option-(ii) spec and deterministic unit fixtures using mocked primitives; verify the existing shadow path logs the incumbent and failures and never modifies the routing result. No model call or serving route change is part of this prep slice.
findings.inference_acceptance: Run all three CS-24 arms on the frozen CS-4 routing set and compare precision/recall plus end-to-end latency/cost. This remains necessary before a policy choice; fixtures do not establish comparative accuracy.
findings.gate: Local models only. Keep the typed classifier shadow-only until the original CS-4 comparison supports a later decision. Never threshold the reported confidence; host routing remains authoritative.
findings.ownership: Conversation-stack CS-24 owns routing experiment; typed-decision APIs are shared existing primitives. No competing owner identified in the assigned shard.
findings.proposed_handoff_append: **JEV implementation option (acceptance preserved):** define CS-24 option (ii) as the existing local `run_typed_decisions` choice catalogue over the CS-4 routing labels, emitted through `submit_shadow` beside the incumbent decision. Keep the caller route unchanged and confidence logging-only; use deterministic mocked-primitive fixtures for schema/failure behavior. The existing CS-4 three-arm precision/recall and cost comparison remains the acceptance gate.
